gen_risks.description: Intense seasonal rainfall and river flooding may suspend civil works and damage bridge and link road assets during construction.
gen_risks.mitigation: Incorporate climate-resilient engineering standards, elevated bridge soffits, scour protection, and green drainage infrastructure into detailed civil works designs.
gen_risks.evidence: Climate change is projected to intensify the frequency of heavy rainfall events during the rainy season, leading to increased flood risks for riverine communities.

gen_risks.description: High domestic fiscal pressures and macroeconomic inflation may impair the government's ability to provide committed counterpart funding.
gen_risks.mitigation: Ensure counterpart funding commitments are ring-fenced in the national budget and monitor fiscal disbursements alongside IDA grant drawdowns.
gen_risks.evidence: macroeconomic environment, which is characterized by intensified fiscal pressures, soaring inflation driven by global supply shocks, and a slowdown of trade activities.

gen_risks.description: Institutional fragmentation and overlapping mandates among transport agencies may delay project implementation and enforcement.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a National Project Steering Committee chaired by MTA and assign dedicated technical focal points from SLRA and MAFS to the PCIU.
gen_risks.evidence: The institutional framework for transport sector management in Sierra Leone is fragmented and lacks systematic coordination among the multiple agencies operating with overlapping responsibilities.

gen_risks.description: Inadequate road maintenance funding collected by the Road Maintenance Fund Administration may lead to asset deterioration after project completion.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement digital Bridge Management System and RAMS tools while developing a strategic transport plan to reform and enhance road maintenance fund allocations.
gen_risks.evidence: In 2020, the RMFA collected approximately US$12.5 million... which is a small fraction of the actual support needed for road maintenance in Sierra Leone.

gen_risks.description: MTA's lack of experience with World Bank financial management procedures and existing control weaknesses present high operational financial management risks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Recruit a qualified Financial Management Specialist and Internal Auditor, adopt an FM Manual, and procure dedicated accounting software within 90 days.
gen_risks.evidence: The FM risk before considering the mitigating measures is 'High' mainly due to: (i) Insufficient experience of MTA with the World Bank's FM procedures

gen_risks.description: Absence of an established procurement unit in PCIU and low initial staff capacity may lead to procurement delays and non-compliance.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a dedicated procurement unit in PCIU staffed with experienced specialists and mandate the use of STEP with regular World Bank procurement clinics.
gen_risks.evidence: The PCIU does not have a procurement unit currently and it will be established and staffed with a qualified and experienced person before the project effectiveness.

gen_risks.description: A US$7.1 million financing gap on ongoing SCADeP bridge contracts could halt construction if fiscal counterpart funds are delayed.
gen_risks.mitigation: Allocate US$4 million from CAMIP Subcomponent 2b to partially bridge the gap after full SCADeP resource utilization, bound by legal financing conditions.
gen_risks.evidence: This leaves a funding gap of about US$7.1 million which was initially planned to be filled by the GoSL fiscal support.

gen_risks.description: Low private sector participation or lease payment default by private bus operators could disrupt the expanded urban public transport scheme.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct an urban transport market study under PPA to assess operator appetite and structure concession contracts with clear lease payment and ownership transfer terms.
gen_risks.evidence: The progress of the private capital enabling will be monitored with the indicator of number of bus lease agreement signed.

gen_risks.description: Incomplete geotechnical investigations prior to contract award for long-span bridges may cause cost overruns and structural design revisions.
gen_risks.mitigation: Mandate comprehensive post-award geotechnical site investigations and require independent supervision consultants to perform rigorous design reviews before civil works commence.
gen_risks.evidence: Additional geotechnical investigation is proposed for the bridges after the contract award to establish, particularly, the foundation or pile depth.

gen_risks.description: Low digital literacy and limited smartphone access among rural populations, especially women, could hamper the adoption of the upgraded AMIS.
gen_risks.mitigation: Partner with women's organizations and NGOs to deliver digital training and deploy alternative offline channels like IVR systems and community intermediaries.
gen_risks.evidence: exclusive reliance on AMIS mobile apps for accessing data and information could indeed pose a barrier for rural women who have less access to smartphones

gen_risks.description: Civil works and labor influx across rural bridge and urban transport sites create potential risks of sexual exploitation, abuse, and sexual harassment.
gen_risks.mitigation: Adopt and implement an SEA/SH Action Plan, enforce worker codes of conduct, and establish accessible, confidential grievance channels.
gen_risks.evidence: The project will also assess the risks related to SEA/SH and prepare an SH/SEA action plan.

gen_risks.description: Land acquisition and potential physical or economic displacement from bridge, road, and market construction may trigger local disputes or project delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Update, disclose, and implement Resettlement Action Plans (RAPs) prior to works and establish functional local Grievance Redress Mechanisms.
gen_risks.evidence: consultations... gather all concerns on various issues relating to potential relocation of the project-affected people and sitting of the proposed bridges and agricultural market infrastructure.

gen_risks.description: Weak local council administrative capacity and poor fee collection mechanisms could lead to inadequate maintenance and decay of agricultural market infrastructure.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide tailored training on revenue management and asset maintenance planning to local councils, market committees, and market queens.
gen_risks.evidence: local councils are responsible for the establishment and administration of market centers... councils will establish a revenue collection system to generate funds for future maintenance

gen_risks.description: Failure to fulfill legal covenants and post-effectiveness conditions within stipulated deadlines could cause disbursement suspensions and project startup delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Monitor compliance milestones through a dedicated legal tracking matrix and leverage PPA resources to advance key deliverables prior to effectiveness.
gen_risks.evidence: No later than ninety (90) days after the Effective Date... the Recipient shall have: (i) identified and procured appropriate software for use in Project accounting

gen_risks.description: Inflexible traffic enforcement and lack of synchronized road safety data may impair the operation of bus priority lanes and road safety measures.
gen_risks.mitigation: Finance national road safety guidelines, create a synchronized database with SLRSA, and support policy enforcement through the newly established SLPTA.
gen_risks.evidence: Sierra Leone has one of the poorest road safety records globally with ineffective monitoring system and weak enforcement.

gen_risks.description: Activation of the Contingent Emergency Response Component due to severe natural disasters would reallocate funds away from planned project components.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop a CERC Manual and Emergency Action Plan to regulate activation criteria while maintaining contingency buffers across main components.
gen_risks.evidence: This will allow for rapid reallocation of [loan/credit/grant] uncommitted funds in the event of an eligible emergency as defined in OP 8.00.

gt_risks.description: Political and governance is rated Substantial. This project's activities are not highly sensitive to moderate perturbations in the political dispensation, although pronounced degeneration in political stability could still undermine their implementation. The more likely risk is that poor governance may affect implementation for the road sector, resulting in reduced commitment during implementation.
gt_risks.mitigation: These risks will be mitigated through close supervision, strict adherence to the criteria for beneficiary selection, and fiduciary oversight.

gt_risks.description: Macroeconomic risk is assessed as Substantial. Sierra Leone's post-pandemic recovery was disrupted by concurrent domestic and external shocks. Inflation and exchange rate depreciation reached record levels, depressing economic activity and triggering a severe cost-of-living crisis. Fiscal accounts have deteriorated on account of macroeconomic headwinds and policy slippages, and risks to debt sustainability have intensified. The economy is projected to grow at 3.8 percent on average during 2023-2025, below the long-term trend, and this baseline is vulnerable to downside risks given recent fiscal slippages and expenditure overruns. The macroeconomic risk may raise concerns about contractors' cost overrun and delay of payment.
gt_risks.mitigation: Key macroeconomic reforms will help reduce the imbalances and avoid the downside risks. The project is 100 percent financed by IDA which will help mitigate the macroeconomic challenges to project implementation.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risk is rated Substantial. The key fiduciary risks are related to the overall governance context of the project, the risk that procurement of project works may be delayed and/or result in higher-than-expected bid prices or poorly performing contractors, and difficulty retaining qualified procurement and FM professionals in the PCIU.
gt_risks.mitigation: These risks will be mitigated by implementing an action plan that aims to strengthen the accountability and control framework for project implementation and improve overall fiduciary performance, and by ensuring adequate procurement and FM training. The PPSD will establish appropriate prequalification requirements and adopt standard lessons from experience procuring similar works contracts in Sierra Leone. The FM risk will be further mitigated by recruiting an internal auditor under PCIU.

gt_risks.description: The project's E&S risk is Substantial (para 74, explicitly pointing to section V.D for detail - para 74 states both environment risk and social risk are rated Substantial 'as indicated in section V.D'). Section V.D (paras 64-68): overall E&S risk classification is Substantial, with eight of ten Environmental and Social Standards (ESS) applying. Environmental risk is Substantial: construction activities are expected to generate air/noise nuisance, construction waste, and traffic/worker safety issues, and Component 2 in particular could affect downstream water users (water quality/hydrology, navigation, fish catch, riparian vegetation), with some impacts potentially long-term or irreversible (e.g. accidental spill of used oil/electrolytes/hazardous materials into the river during construction). Social risk is also Substantial: key risks include physical and economic displacement of boat/ferry operators, loaders, and traders after bridge construction; SEA/SH risks from the contractor workforce; elite capture in market-infrastructure interventions; social exclusion of vulnerable groups (persons with disabilities, women/small traders, the landless, elders); and secondary risks including potential child labor, communicable-disease spread from the contractor workforce, and local conflict over benefit-sharing from downstream impacts.
gt_risks.mitigation: Standard measures per the ESIA/ESMP to be prepared for project activities, including energy-efficiency measures per World Bank EHS Guidelines/GIIPs; a site-specific SEA/SH risk assessment and commensurate GBV/SEA/SH action plan; the Environmental and Social Commitment Plan (ESCP) and Stakeholder Engagement Plan (SEP), disclosed April 19, 2024; hiring a social specialist with GBV/SEA/SH experience before project effectiveness; an ESIA and Resettlement Action Plan/livelihoods restoration plan already under development for the seven originally-planned bridges, with updated ESIA/ESMP/RAP and a SEA/SH action plan to be disclosed within one month of effectiveness; and a functional grievance mechanism (GM) plus Labor Management Procedures (LMP) for project workers.
